atlas.atlas_note: Argentina's main wine province, producing most of the country's wine in an irrigated high desert at the foot of the Andes. Malbec is its signature.

study.lesson: Southern Hemisphere path, 'Argentina: altitude, Malbec and Torrontés'
facts: Vineyards in the Andean rain shadow, irrigated with Andean snowmelt
Primera Zona = Luján de Cuyo and Maipú
Luján de Cuyo and San Rafael are the DOCs (1999 law: IP, IG, DOC)
Valle de Uco = Tupungato, Tunuyán, San Carlos; in the Valle de Uco many vineyards lie above 1,000 m
Temperature falls about 0.6 C per 100 m; height lets growers make fresh wines
Hail: many vineyards use nets; Zonda, hot dry wind from the Andes, can damage flowering in spring
Michel Aimé Pouget brought Malbec to Mendoza in the mid-nineteenth century
Bonarda is the second red grape
